stem: A model is configured with `materialized='incremental'`. Its SQL must stay valid whether the run is incremental or not, and the team needs the name of the built-in Jinja macro that evaluates to `True` only when the destination table already exists, the full-refresh flag was not passed, and the model is configured as incremental. Name the macro, with parentheses: ____
drill_answer_short: is_incremental() returns True only when all three conditions hold
decision_hinge: The is_incremental() macro will return True if all of the following conditions are met: the model already exists as a table in the database, the full-refresh flag is not passed, and the running model is configured with materialized='incremental'.

stem: A model's `.sql` file has a `{{ config(materialized='view') }}` block. The model also has a `schema.yml` config property setting a different materialization, and the project's `dbt_project.yml` sets a project-wide default materialization plus a folder-level override, and all three layers disagree on the materialization. The team must determine which one dbt actually builds. Which layer wins, and why?

option_texts.A: dbt builds the model as the `schema.yml` property states, because a `.yml` resource property is the innermost layer dbt reads
option_texts.B: dbt builds the model as the in-file block states, because that layer is nested deepest and wins over the schema property and project settings
option_texts.C: dbt builds the model as the project-wide default states, because `dbt_project.yml` settings apply to every model regardless of folder
option_texts.D: dbt raises a compilation error, because the layers disagree and dbt cannot resolve the conflict on its own

drill_answer_short: The in-file config() block is the most specific layer and always wins
decision_hinge: Model configurations are applied hierarchically: a config() Jinja macro within a model file takes precedence over a config resource property in a .yml file, which takes precedence over the project YAML file; the most specific configuration always takes precedence, and in the project YAML file a subdirectory takes precedence over the entire project.

plausible_options.A: also has a `schema.yml` config property setting a different materialization

eliminated_by.C: the project's `dbt_project.yml` sets a project-wide default materialization plus a folder-level override
eliminated_by.D: and all three layers disagree on the materialization

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling — the resource property is real but sits between the in-file config block and the project file in the precedence order, not above the in-file block
distractor_traps.C: T8: scope error — a project-wide default is the least specific layer, not a tiebreaker
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — dbt resolves config precedence deterministically; a conflicting hierarchy is not a parse failure
